# ghost_organization_settings (Resource)

Manages an organization's settings: its base permission, repository policies and public profile. There is one per organization, and you must be an admin of it. Every argument is optional: an argument you leave out is left as it is in Ghost and isn't managed, and taking an argument out of the configuration stops managing it without changing it. **Destroying the resource doesn't change any settings**: it only removes them from the Terraform state. The organization's display name and logo can't be changed here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every argument is optional: the ones you leave out stay as they are.
# Destroying the resource leaves the settings unchanged.
resource "ghost_organization_settings" "example" {
  organization = "my-org"

  # Members can read every repository; "none" gives them nothing beyond
  # their teams and collaborations.
  base_permission                         = "read"
  members_can_create_public_repositories  = false
  members_can_create_private_repositories = true
  allow_private_forks                     = false
  oauth_app_restrictions                  = true

  # New repositories start on this branch.
  default_branch = "main"

  # The public profile. "" clears a field.
  description = "Rockets and other things that go up"
  website     = "https://my-org.example"
  location    = "Earth"
  email       = ""
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `organization` (String) The organization's slug, matched case-insensitively and kept as configured. Changing it to another organization forces a new resource (which leaves the old organization's settings as they are); changing only its case doesn't.

### Optional

- `allow_private_forks` (Boolean) Whether the organization's private repositories can be forked. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `base_permission` (String) Every member's role on every repository: `read`, `triage`, `write`, `maintain` or `admin`, or `none` to give members nothing beyond their teams and collaborations. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `default_branch` (String) The default branch of each new repository, at most 255 characters. Ghost doesn't check that it's a valid branch name, and existing repositories keep theirs. Set it to `""` to clear it. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `description` (String) The description on the organization's profile, at most 350 characters. Set it to `""` to clear it. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `email` (String) The public email address on the organization's profile. Set it to `""` to clear it. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `location` (String) The location on the organization's profile, at most 100 characters. Set it to `""` to clear it. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `members_can_create_private_repositories` (Boolean) Whether members can create private repositories. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `members_can_create_public_repositories` (Boolean) Whether members can create public repositories. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `oauth_app_restrictions` (Boolean) Whether OAuth apps reach the organization's repositories only once an admin approves them. Apps built into Ghost, such as `gh`, and the organization's own apps are always allowed. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.
- `website` (String) The website on the organization's profile. Ghost requires a URL with a scheme, such as `https://example.com`. Set it to `""` to clear it. Leave it out to leave the setting unmanaged.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The organization's slug, in lower case.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Organization settings are imported by the organization's slug.
terraform import ghost_organization_settings.example my-org
```
